excl.s: New Ramp data shows AI spend growth slowed sharply over the past two months; Ramp's economist points to falling prices for frontier models.
Total AI spend on Ramp is falling even as token volumes rise, as OpenAI and Anthropic compete on price. Top-1% spend per employee fell nearly 10% from July to August.
Ramp card and bill-pay data show 13.3% of U.S. healthcare businesses and 10% of finance and insurance firms on Ramp paid a fax-service provider in the first nine months of 2026.
excl.t: Faxing into the future: top industries paying for fax services

items.t: Truckload contract rate increases riding steady above 10%
items.s: Contract truckload rates are still running more than 10% above year-ago levels, a sign shippers face persistently higher freight costs heading into 2027 bid season.

items.t: Record tanker rates cripple U.S. crude oil flows to Asia
items.s: Soaring charter costs for supertankers have made shipping American crude to Asian buyers uneconomic, cutting export flows.

items.t: Will AI expose the rickety infrastructure of the internet?
items.s: After a run of critical web vulnerabilities, TechCrunch examines whether AI-driven bug hunting and traffic will strain aging internet software that businesses depend on.

items.t: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn't make it
items.s: A tally of AI products and startups that have shut down, highlighting the shakeout as funding concentrates in a few leaders.
The Fed, ECB and Bank of Japan are all expected to hold rates next week, with the Fed keeping a hawkish tone as markets bet on a December hike.
items.t: Fed set to lead G7 trio in hawkish rate pause: Eco Week Ahead

items.s: Singapore high-sulphur fuel oil now costs more than crude as lost Middle East and Russian supply and steep freight rates squeeze Asia's shipping-fuel market.
items.t: Fuel oil becomes Asia's next cost shock

items.s: American hoarding before tariffs has left Quebec's strategic maple syrup reserve close to empty.
items.t: Quebec's maple syrup reserves are nearly drained after U.S. buyers stockpiled ahead of tariffs

items.s: A top economist argues the AI investment thesis has a fundamental weakness as data-center financing strains show up in credit markets.
items.t: Here's the 'core economic flaw' in the AI bull case as stock and bond trades unravel

items.s: A new report finds about half of workers have quit abruptly without notice, and most of them were long-tenured, loyal employees.
items.t: Half of workers are 'revenge quitting' and walking out on their jobs without notice

items.s: Volkswagen is preparing to build an Audi factory in Georgia, giving the brand US production as tariffs push automakers to localize manufacturing.
items.t: Volkswagen plans new Audi plant in Georgia, handing Trump a win

items.s: A prominent AI skeptic argues GPU shortages are manufactured by Nvidia's pricing strategy rather than real demand limits, adding to doubts behind this week's tech selloff.
items.t: AI bear slams Nvidia's GPU pitch: 'There's not scarcity other than that which is created by Jensen Huang'

items.s: Telecom executives and analysts say SpaceX faces years of spectrum, regulatory and infrastructure hurdles before it can seriously challenge wireless carriers.
items.t: SpaceX's telecom ambitions will be hard-won, CEOs and analysts say

items.s: UK officials are monitoring the discount chain's finances amid fears of store closures and job losses as weak consumer spending squeezes retailers.
items.t: Government on alert over potential Poundland crisis

items.s: HSBC has rolled a stablecoin out to millions of retail customers in Hong Kong, one of the largest bank-led pushes of digital dollars into mainstream payments.
items.t: Hong Kong's biggest bank puts a stablecoin in 3 million wallets

items.s: A pair of severe flaws in PHP, which runs much of the web, forced a scramble to patch servers and highlighted how AI tools are speeding up the discovery of exploitable bugs.
items.t: How two critical PHP web bugs almost broke the internet

items.s: Unrest spread beyond France as Italy deployed 500 more soldiers to Milan after looting that led to 45 arrests, while protests were called in at least seven more cities, including a Madrid pensions march ahead of Spain's snap election.
items.t: It's not just France — Protesters are marching across Europe as part of the newly formed 'Oct. 17 Movement'

items.s: Moody's held France at Aa3 with a negative outlook but warned that political gridlock leaves public debt, now a record 119% of GDP, on track for 122% next year, with the 2027 deficit likely only trimmed to about 5.2%.
items.t: France's latest debt warning describes a country where governance is breaking down — and even doing too little, too late is barely possible

items.s: An AP report says nearly every U.S. transit system still needs a human operator, but D.C. Metro's roughly $1 billion Red Line upgrade could run trains with no one in the cab by 2033, and Los Angeles is studying a fully automated line.
items.t: The U.S. lags far behind on using driverless trains, but new projects could open the floodgates

items.s: NASA says a roughly two-week, four-astronaut Artemis III docking test next summer will pair Orion with Blue Origin's lander before SpaceX's Starship, with the first crewed landing still slated for 2028.
items.t: Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin will face off in orbit next year, NASA confirms

items.s: NielsenIQ data show Halloween candy sales down 6.7% year over year in the month to Oct. 17, with only small bags growing as $4.29 gas (up nearly 40%) and candy prices up 44% in five years squeeze shoppers.
items.t: America skimps on Halloween as high fuel prices force shoppers to buy small bags of candy and abandon large sizes

items.s: A Nationwide survey finds 72% of Gen Z investors adjusted retirement portfolios ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms versus 17% of boomers, while advisers point to average S&P 500 gains of about 15% in the year after midterms since 1950.
items.t: Gen Z is treating the midterms like a market event. Boomers are treating them like weather

items.s: AI voice-cloning scams are spreading as a three-second clip can yield an 85% voice match, with an estimated 15 million U.S. adults losing about $68 billion to scams in 2025 and 12% of reported scams involving AI or deepfakes.
items.t: Scammers used AI to clone her daughter's voice and fake a kidnapping. A voice expert says every family now needs a safe word

items.s: Instacart held early talks about a possible sale with delivery rivals DoorDash and Uber, according to a report.
items.t: Instacart reportedly discussed selling itself with DoorDash and Uber

items.s: Block has released a voice AI model whose speech is strikingly natural, extending the payments company's push into AI.
items.t: Block's new voice model sounds eerily human

items.s: Commodity trading houses are heading for another record year in metals as volatile prices and supply disruptions widen trading margins.
items.t: Metals traders reap bonanza with another year of record profits

items.s: Borrowing costs for German homebuyers have hit a 17-year high as the Iran war and oil spike push up inflation expectations and bond yields.
items.t: German mortgage rates climb to highest since 2009 as Iran war stokes inflation fears

items.s: US households' equity allocation as a share of financial assets has reached a record, topping the 2000 peak.
items.t: Americans have never had more of their money in stocks — not even in the dot-com bubble

items.s: A study forcing AI models to name a candidate in nearly 500 midterm races found Grok backed Republicans 92% of the time and OpenAI's model backed Democrats 97% of the time.
items.t: Forced to pick, Grok's AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI's picks Democrats.

items.s: The designation opens more federal financing to helium producers and brings closer monitoring of a gas essential to chipmaking.
items.t: US designates helium as a critical material, citing its importance for semiconductors

items.s: Google, Meta and others are offering communities bigger incentives and more transparency as local opposition to data centers grows.
items.t: Facing pushback on data centers, tech giants are promising hosts more money and fewer secrets

items.s: Plywood, packing crates and some machinery from Canada will be exempt from the 50% tariffs starting Oct. 30, a move seen as helping Maine Sen. Susan Collins.
items.t: Trump exempts some Canadian imports from his 50% tariffs

items.s: Daytona, which provides cloud sandboxes for running AI agents, reached unicorn status with backing from FirstMark and a roster of prominent angel investors.
items.t: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation

items.s: The lab-testing giant said attackers accessed patient personal and medical information, the latest in a string of major cyber incidents this week.
items.t: Quest Diagnostics confirms patients' personal and health data was compromised in breach

items.s: A tanker carrying Russian diesel is bound for New York under the new US-Russia fuel arrangement, the first such shipment since 2023 as the Iran war strains supplies.
items.t: First Russian diesel tanker under Trump-Putin deal heads to New York

items.s: Shortly after the open the Dow was down about 1% and the S&P 500 0.4% as AI stocks extended Thursday's rout, while AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile fell 3% to 4.7% on a report that SpaceX is exploring a nationwide wireless carrier.
items.t: Wall St dips after AI-led selloff; SpaceX worries hit telecoms

items.s: Stocks closed lower Friday as AI-spending worries and U.S. crude topping $100 weighed: the Dow fell about 653 points (1.2%) to 52,215, the S&P 500 slid 0.5% and the Nasdaq 0.2%, leaving both down for a second straight week.
items.t: Stock market today: Dow sinks 600 points, S&P 500, Nasdaq drop to cap a volatile week, oil prices rise

items.s: Omnicom says its Interpublic integration is largely done and it remains on track for $900 million in cost savings this year, posting 7.2% organic Q3 growth to $6 billion as it won Coca-Cola's North American media but lost PepsiCo to Publicis.
items.t: Omnicom-IPG deal ‘substantially completed’ as group wins Coke’s NA media

items.s: Brent climbed about 1.5% to near $115 a barrel, its highest since early May and headed for a third straight weekly gain, as Middle East attacks, a tanker spill off the UAE and a Libyan pipeline shutdown stoked supply fears; WTI rose to about $101.
items.t: Brent crude hits more than five-month high on Houthi-Saudi attacks, UAE oil spill

items.s: After the Nasdaq's worst day since June, investors face reports from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon plus a Fed meeting next week, with hyperscaler capex near $800 billion this year, Q3 S&P 500 earnings tracking up over 32%, and futures pricing about an 80% chance of a December rate hike.
items.t: Earnings flood, Fed meeting pose pivotal tests for rickety AI market rally

items.s: CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts after third-quarter results that AmEx will eliminate about 5% of its global staff, booking a roughly $336 million restructuring charge, and shares fell nearly 3% in early trading.
items.t: American Express is cutting 5% of its workforce to 'prepare for AI'

items.s: Volvo Cars stock fell close to 30% after the Geely-controlled automaker swung to a 5.7 billion kronor quarterly loss on a 23% revenue drop, blaming U.S. tariffs and Chinese competition, and announced about 2,500 job cuts and a 5 billion kronor savings plan.
items.t: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts

items.s: Brent rose another 0.9% to about $114.73 a barrel on Friday after a 4% jump Thursday, with Gulf-to-Asia crude shipping now over five times pre-war costs and the U.S. 10-year yield back below 5%.
items.t: Oil tops $114 as European shares fall and Kering tumbles

items.s: Global markets were mixed Friday after a Nasdaq drop of 2.6% led by Nvidia (-4.4%), Meta (-7%) and CoreWeave (-10%), while the 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.97% from 5.13% and European indexes opened lower.
items.t: World shares are mixed after Wall Street's AI-related losses, while oil prices jump

items.s: OpenAI is stopping training on freshly scraped web content, saying the open internet now poses too many risks to model quality and safety.
items.t: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing significant risks

items.s: Sportsbooks have poured more than $80 million into races through a PAC, while prediction-market firms Kalshi and Polymarket are also stepping up political and lobbying spending.
items.t: Betting operators and prediction markets spent record amounts on campaign donations and lobbying

items.s: Treasuries rallied as doubts over AI profitability and infrastructure spending spread, with an HSBC survey finding most investors expect AI capex to slow meaningfully within a year.
items.t: US Treasurys gained in investors' flight to safety

items.s: A former Justice Department official says a Musk-floated Tesla-SpaceX combination could draw antitrust review over fears rivals would be shut out of SpaceX technology like Starlink.
items.t: SpaceX-Tesla merger could face antitrust scrutiny

items.s: The two firms are teaming up to simplify tender offers, which have tripled for late-stage startups over three years but remain rare, with just 44 executed in their data in the first half of 2026.
items.t: Carta and NewView partner to get more startups to let employees sell shares early

items.s: Meta is creating nonvoting shares it can sell to raise money for its AI buildout while keeping Mark Zuckerberg's voting control intact.
items.t: Meta's new class of nonvoting stock lets Zuckerberg fund AI without losing control

items.s: Investor jitters over AI spending are pushing up the borrowing cost of SpaceX's planned $40 billion debt raise.
items.t: SpaceX $40 billion debt deal gets pricey as AI fears spread

items.s: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back on worries that AI investment has become a bubble amid a volatile week for tech stocks.
items.t: US Treasury Secretary Bessent dismisses AI bubble fears

items.s: Barclays is shedding about 5,000 jobs, roughly 5% of staff, crediting AI efficiencies: 1,000 roles are already gone and 4,000 more go by year-end, mostly in UK retail banking, as Q3 pre-tax profit rose 12% but missed estimates.
items.t: Barclays layoffs today: Bank attributes 5,000 job cuts to AI

items.s: The Nasdaq closed down 2.6% at 26,008.86, its worst day since early June, and the S&P 500 fell 1.2% while the Dow ended flat, as chip stocks sank 6.7% on AI-spending doubts after Meta fell 7% and Houthi strikes pushed oil to a five-month high.
items.t: S&P 500, Nasdaq end sharply lower as revived AI doubts ignite tech selloff

items.s: The Nasdaq closed down 2.6% at 26,008 and the S&P 500 fell 1.2% while the Dow ended flat, as Meta dropped 7% on its $135B-$145B capex outlook, Tesla slid 3.1%, P&G jumped 5.6%, and WTI crude rose 3% to about $100.
items.t: Nasdaq Sinks 694 Points as Meta Stock Slumps After Earnings: Stock Market Today

items.s: Elon Musk has reportedly put roughly $1 billion into Skydance, the media company formed by Paramount Skydance's $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, as part of a wider equity raise.
items.t: Elon Musk invests about $1B in Skydance, CNBC reports

items.s: Chemical maker Dow posted operating earnings of 71 cents a share versus a year-earlier loss, with sales up 13% and net income rising to $525 million as price increases and cost cuts outran higher raw-material and logistics costs.
items.t: Dow beat earnings expectations as profit jumped on higher prices, cost cuts

items.s: U.S. stocks slid Thursday with the Nasdaq down more than 2% as Meta fell about 8% on AI-spending worries, chip stocks sank and Brent crude topped $111 on Middle East tensions.
items.t: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq tumble as tech stocks sink, Meta plummets 8%

items.s: First-time unemployment filings dipped to 194,000 in the week ended Oct. 17, beating the 200,000 forecast, though continuing claims ticked up.
items.t: US Initial Jobless Claims Fall to Three-Month Low of 194,000

items.s: American now expects a 2026 adjusted loss of $1.00 to $1.60 a share after a $269 million third-quarter loss, even as revenue rose 19% to $16.3 billion on higher fares; shares fell 3.5% premarket.
items.t: American Airlines forecasts 2026 loss as fuel costs outpace fare gains

items.s: Thursday's session turned lower, led by the Nasdaq, as investors balked at Big Tech AI capex plans after Meta and Tesla results while oil prices climbed on Middle East risk.
items.t: Nasdaq tumbles on AI spending concerns and jump in oil prices: Live updates
